html:
Caral is an ancient city in the Supe valley of Peru, about 180 kilometres north of Lima, built from about 2600 BCE. It is the oldest known city in the Americas.

It belongs to the Norte Chico culture of the central coast. Caral had six large platform mounds, sunken circular plazas and houses for perhaps a few thousand people. Its people had no pottery and no evidence of war has been found. They grew cotton, squash and beans with irrigation, and traded cotton nets with fishing towns on the coast for anchovies and shellfish. A knotted cord found there may be an early form of the quipu.

The Peruvian archaeologist Ruth Shady excavated it from 1994 and showed how old it was. It became a World Heritage Site in 2009. It shows that cities arose in Peru as early as in Mesopotamia or Egypt, thousands of years before the Inca.
sum: Caral is an ancient city in the Supe valley of Peru, about 180 kilometres north of Lima, built from about 2600 BCE. It is the oldest known city in the Americas.
